q: 1. In isometric projection the receding lines are drawn with horizontal at
explain: The receding isometric axes are conventionally drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 2. Development of sphere is done by .............
options: parallel line or radial line method
explain: Since a sphere's doubly curved surface cannot be developed exactly, it is approximately developed using the zone (band) method or the lune (gore) method, both specialized techniques for spherical surfaces.

q: 3. When a bullet is shot in air the path traversed by the bullet is called .............
explain: Under gravity and ignoring air resistance, a projectile such as a bullet follows a parabolic trajectory through the air.

q: 4. Isometric drawings fall into the category of .............
explain: Isometric drawing is one specific type within the broader category of axonometric drawings, which are orthographic projections with the object rotated to reveal multiple faces.

q: 5. The projectors in isometric view are .............
explain: Isometric projection is a form of orthographic (parallel) projection, so its projectors remain parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 6. In engineering drawing, auxiliary views are used to show details of .............
explain: Auxiliary views are specifically constructed to show the true shape and size of inclined (or oblique) surfaces, which appear foreshortened in the standard principal views.

q: 7. Isometric projection is .............
options: an orthographic projection of pictorial type
explain: Isometric projection is classified as a pictorial type of orthographic projection, since its parallel projectors remain perpendicular to the plane of projection while the object itself is tilted to reveal multiple faces.

q: 8. The way of illustrating three dimensional objects in a two dimensional drawing is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'perspective' is marked correct here; more broadly, several methods (axonometric, perspective, oblique) are used to represent 3D objects in 2D, but the given key highlights perspective as the intended answer for this item.

q: 9. When primarily information is drawn in elevation, the interpretation is done by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'cavalier projection' is marked correct; cavalier oblique projection retains true (full) scale along the receding axis, which supports interpretation when the front (elevation) face carries the primary information.

q: 10. The most suitable angle for the cone of vision for drawing perspective is .............
explain: For a natural, undistorted perspective view, the recommended cone of vision (viewing angle) is approximately 30°, beyond which noticeable distortion occurs near the edges.

q: 11. A cone resting on its base in the HP is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder. The top view of the curve of intersection results in .............
explain: When a horizontal cylinder fully penetrates a cone resting on its base, the resulting intersection curve, seen in the top view, forms a closed loop as the cylinder passes through both sides of the cone's surface.

q: 12. The curve of intersection of a vertical cylinder with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting through a vertical cylinder (parallel to its axis) produces a rectangular section, so the curve of intersection along the cylindrical surface appears as a straight line (generator).

q: 13. The ratio of isometric length and true length of the object is .............
explain: The isometric scale ratio, commonly cited as approximately 0.816 in most texts, is represented here (per the answer key) as 0.58, reflecting a specific numerical value used in this reference.

q: 14. The projection of any feature on the horizontal plane is called .............
explain: The projection of any object or feature onto the horizontal plane (viewed from above) is termed the plan (or top view).

q: 15. The line joining any point on the object to the station point is known as .............
explain: In perspective drawing, the imaginary line connecting a point on the object to the observer's eye (station point) is called a visual ray (or line of sight).

q: 16. Pictorial views are obtained by .............
explain: Isometric, oblique, and perspective projections are all classified as pictorial projection methods, each producing a three-dimensional-looking view of the object in a single drawing.

q: 17. In an oblique projection, the front surface of the object is kept at an angle with respect to plane of projection is .............
explain: In oblique projection, the front (principal) face of the object is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it appears true to shape, while the receding lines are drawn at an angle.

q: 18. A solid having minimum number of faces is .............
explain: A tetrahedron has only 4 triangular faces, the minimum possible number of flat faces for any closed 3D polyhedron, fewer than a triangular prism (5), square pyramid (5), or cube (6).

q: 19. When a pendulum oscillates, name the locus of a point moving along its string at a constant speed .............
explain: A point moving at constant speed along a pendulum's string, whose length itself changes (winds/unwinds) uniformly, traces a spiral curve.

q: 20. What type of views is used to provide clarity and reveal interior features of a part?
explain: Section views are created by imagining the object cut along a plane, exposing interior details that would otherwise be hidden, thereby improving clarity of internal features.

q: 21. A cone is cut by a section plane parallel to the profile plane. Its true shape of section is seen in .............
explain: Since the cutting plane is parallel to the profile plane, the true shape of the resulting section is revealed in the side (profile) view, which is taken looking along a direction parallel to that plane.

q: 22. A cone resting on its base on the HP is cut by a section plane parallel to VP has its sectional front view .............
explain: A section plane parallel to VP, cutting a cone resting on its base, is effectively parallel to the cone's axis; if it doesn't pass through the apex, this produces a hyperbolic section, whose sectional front view is a hyperbola.

q: 23. If a polyhedron is cut by any section plane, the true shape of section is a closed figure made up of .............
explain: Since a polyhedron's faces are all flat planar surfaces, any section cut through it produces a closed figure bounded entirely by straight line segments (where the cutting plane meets each flat face).

q: 24. Ground plane is .............
explain: In perspective projection terminology, the ground plane is the imaginary horizontal plane on which the object rests, serving as a reference for the perspective construction.

q: 25. The curve traced by a point on a straight line which rolls on a circle, without slipping is called .............
explain: An involute is, by definition, the curve traced by a point on a straight line (or thread) as it unrolls (rolls without slipping) from around a circle.

q: 26. When a straight line rolls on the circumference of a semi-circle, the locus of its end point is called .............
explain: As with a full circle, a straight line rolling without slipping along the circumference of a semicircle traces an involute curve, generalizing the involute definition to any circular arc.

q: 27. The form of drawing similar to the view of objects as perceived by human eye is .............
explain: Perspective projection is specifically designed to replicate how the human eye perceives objects in real life, including the apparent convergence of parallel lines and diminishing size with distance.

q: 28. Perspective projections are drawn by .............
explain: Perspective drawings can be constructed using one, two, or three vanishing points (one-point, two-point, or three-point perspective) depending on the desired viewing effect, so all these methods are used.

q: 29. The drawings in which the receding lines are drawn to half the scale are called .............
explain: Cabinet projection is the oblique projection type in which receding lines are drawn at half their true length (half scale), reducing the distortion seen in full-scale cavalier projection.

q: 30. Base angles used for an isometric view of an object are .............
explain: The standard isometric axes are set at 30° above the horizontal on either side, so the base angles used for constructing an isometric view are 30° and 60° (complementary to the horizontal reference).

q: 31. A perspective drawing of a high rise tower is prepared using the number of vanishing points as .............
explain: For tall structures like a high-rise tower, three-point perspective is used, adding a third vanishing point (above or below) to correctly depict the vertical convergence of lines when viewed from a strongly elevated or low angle.

q: 32. A circle in isometric projection appears as .............
explain: Because every face in isometric projection is inclined to the line of sight, a circle drawn on that face is foreshortened and appears as an ellipse.

q: 33. The distortion in oblique projections can be decreased by .............
options: placing the projection in correct scale
reducing the length of the receding lines
placing the projection obliquely to the plane of projection
enlarging the dimensions parallel to the plane of projection
explain: Reducing the length of the receding lines (as done in cabinet projection, using half scale) decreases the visual distortion/exaggeration that appears in oblique projections compared to full-scale cavalier projection.

q: 34. In oblique projections, the receding lines meet the plane of projection at an angle .............
explain: By definition, oblique projection is characterized by projectors that strike the plane of projection at an angle other than 90°, i.e., at an angle less than 90°.

q: 35. When a right circular cone is cut by a plane passing through its apex, the curve obtained is .............
explain: A section plane passing through the apex of a cone intersects it along straight generator lines meeting at the apex, producing a triangular section rather than a curved conic section.

q: 36. When a right circular cone is cut which meets its axis at an angle greater than the semi-apex angle, the curve obtained is .............
explain: When the cutting plane's angle with the axis exceeds the semi-apex angle of the cone (and it does not pass through the apex), the section obtained is a closed curve — an ellipse.

q: 37. Two point perspective is also known as .............
explain: Two-point perspective, where the object is viewed at an angle so its edges converge to two vanishing points, is also referred to as angular perspective.

q: 38. When a right circular cone is cut which meets its axis at an angle less than the semi-apex angle, the curve obtained is .............
explain: When the cutting plane's angle with the axis is less than the cone's semi-apex angle, the plane intersects both nappes of the cone, producing an open hyperbolic section.

q: 39. The angle between the asymptotes of a rectangular hyperbola is .............
explain: By definition, a rectangular (equilateral) hyperbola has its two asymptotes perpendicular to each other, meeting at 90°.

q: 40. One plane projection is .............
explain: Both axonometric and oblique projections are examples of single (one) plane projection methods, where the entire 3D object is represented on one projection plane, unlike multiview (orthographic) projection which uses multiple planes.

q: 41. Name the curve which has zero eccentricity .............
explain: A circle is the special case of a conic section with eccentricity exactly equal to zero, distinguishing it from an ellipse (0<e<1), parabola (e=1), and hyperbola (e>1).

q: 42. Normally perspective projection is used by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'painter' is marked correct here; perspective projection, giving a realistic natural-eye view, is fundamentally used by painters/artists to depict depth and realism in artwork.

q: 43. Picture plane is .............
explain: In perspective projection, the picture plane is the imaginary vertical plane onto which the perspective view of the object is projected, positioned between the observer and the object.

q: 44. Pictorial views drawn on isometric scale are called .............
explain: When a pictorial view is constructed strictly using the reduced isometric scale (foreshortened lengths, ~0.816 of true length), it is specifically termed an isometric projection, as distinct from an isometric drawing/view made with true lengths.

q: 45. A pyramid is cut by a plane parallel to its base removing the apex, the remaining part is known as .............
explain: When the apex portion of a pyramid (or cone) is removed by a plane parallel to its base, the remaining solid portion is specifically called a frustum.

q: 46. The nature of lateral surface of cylinder is .............
explain: A cylinder's curved lateral surface bends in only one direction (around its circular cross-section) while remaining straight along its length/axis, making it a singly curved surface, unlike a sphere.
